newsitem.title: USA: Regis see Q2 EPS below consensus.
newsitem.headline: Regis see Q2 EPS below consensus.

text.p: Regis Corp President Paul Finkelstein said Friday the company will not meet the consensus of analysts' earnings estimates for the fiscal second quarter of $0.30 a share.
"We know we're not going to make the $0.30," Finkelstein said.
Asked what earnings for the second quarter, ending in December, are likely to be, he said, "It's premature."
"We feel at this point in time that $0.20 to $0.25 (a share) seems to be realistic, but too much of the month is still left," he added.
Finkelstein said the preliminary earnings projection compares with earnings for the year-ago quarter of $0.17 a share.
Piper Jaffray analyst Saul Yaari said the year-ago earnings are restated for Regis' acquisition of Supercuts Inc.
Finkelstein said the shortfall in earnings relates to a smaller than expected increase in same-store sales for the second quarter.
He added that same-store sales likely will increase by 1-1/2 percent, compared with earlier expectations of 2-1/2 to three percent.
The shortfall in same-store sales were due largely to disappointing sales of hair care products at its salons.
"I think it's competition," Finkelstein said. "A lot more people are selling shampoo in malls."
Finkelstein said he expects Regis, which has about 3,200 hair salons, to report earnings for fiscal 1997 that are above 1996, but did not elaborate.
Shares of Regis were down 4-1/2 at 16-3/4.
